method: Review every one of the 392 generic authority cases by primary constitutional/statutory or responsible-institution evidence. Shared frameworks classify the named class only. Separate scope decisions from current institutional activity, player validation and publication. Preserve specific missing-instrument/grant holds and historical succession; do not assert that all legal questions are resolved.

frameworks.assessment: The current Local Government Act Articles 2, 25–28 and 35–36 establishes first-level councils’ autonomous ordinances, including rules affecting residents’ rights/obligations and administrative penalties, budgets and executive questioning. The Presidency explicitly identifies six special municipalities, thirteen counties and three cities as the first self-governing tier and their councils as legislative branches. These 22 qualify under the regional-ordinance rule; township councils and obsolete provincial consultative bodies do not follow by analogy.
frameworks.source_review: Primary constitutional/statutory text or the responsible institution’s description; translated text and source-version limitations are identified below.
frameworks.limitations: Use the current Chinese Act (amended 3 December 2025), not the original Constitution’s now-inapplicable elected provincial assembly model. First-level special/county-equivalent cities are assessed in that statutory capacity, not as an exception for any large municipality.

frameworks.assessment: Constitution Article 104 distinguishes higher territorial self-government and gives its assemblies generally binding ordinances. The Regions Act 129/2000 separates independent regional legislation from delegated state administration and reserves ordinances and budget to the elected assembly. These regional assemblies meet the substantive regional-ordinance rule. Prague qualifies in its combined regional capacity under Act 131/2000, not every municipal council.
frameworks.source_review: Primary constitutional/statutory text or the responsible institution’s description; translated text and source-version limitations are identified below.
frameworks.limitations: The ministry’s English Regions Act is a historical translation, read for the independent/delegated distinction with the constitutional and governmental explanations; not a certification of every current procedural amendment.

frameworks.assessment: Constitution Articles 68–69 and Act 302/2001 sections 8–11 distinguish generally binding regulations in a self-governing region’s own affairs from regulations needing express delegation for state administration. The elected assembly approves regional regulations and budget and elects the chief controller. The eight higher-territorial assemblies qualify under the autonomous regional-ordinance rule, subject to national law.
frameworks.source_review: Primary constitutional/statutory text or the responsible institution’s description; translated text and source-version limitations are identified below.
frameworks.limitations: Framework eligibility does not establish a current official media service; ordinary municipalities remain outside this first-level scope.

frameworks.assessment: Constitution Article 94 and the Voivodeship Self-Government Act Articles 18 and 89 vest elected sejmiki with generally binding regional local-law enactments, budget and executive-control decisions. This qualifies under the regional-ordinance rule, with the explicit statutory limits on lawmaking; it is not sovereign state legislation. A wojewoda’s executive regulations are a different institution.
frameworks.source_review: Primary constitutional/statutory text or the responsible institution’s description; translated text and source-version limitations are identified below.
frameworks.limitations: The 2026 consolidated-text publication establishes the current Act reference; the older HTML provides readable Articles 18/89. Service identity and current regional/chamber particulars remain separate checks.

frameworks.assessment: The Fundamental Law’s local-government decree power is constrained by the allocation of functions. Local Government Act CLXXXIX/2011 section 27 assigns county self-government territorial development, rural development, spatial planning and coordination. These nineteen county assemblies are development/administrative bodies under this project’s service/planning exclusion, rather than autonomous general regional lawmaking parliaments.
frameworks.source_review: Primary constitutional/statutory text or the responsible institution’s description; translated text and source-version limitations are identified below.
frameworks.limitations: This does not deny the legal force of county decrees or their elected/budgetary role. A regional label or planning regulation alone is insufficient.

frameworks.assessment: Budapest’s assembly is the capital municipal self-government under the Fundamental Law and Local Government Act, with citywide services, budget and local decrees. No separate state/autonomous regional legislature is established by that capital status. Apply the ordinary municipal exclusion.
frameworks.source_review: Primary constitutional/statutory text or the responsible institution’s description; translated text and source-version limitations are identified below.

frameworks.assessment: Constitution Articles 135–138 assign counties regional administration of education, public health, planning, development, transport and institutional networks, with statutory self-government and finances. These are local/regional service-administration assemblies; charters and general acts within those assigned tasks do not establish an autonomous regional legislative tier. Zagreb’s combined city/county status does not create a state legislature.
frameworks.source_review: Primary constitutional/statutory text or the responsible institution’s description; translated text and source-version limitations are identified below.
frameworks.limitations: Exclusion is this catalogue’s scope decision, not denial of elected representation or binding administrative acts.

frameworks.assessment: Constitution Article 102 places first- and second-level councils in local administration, with administrative and financial independence and legally allocated local affairs. The thirteen regional councils are that second-level local-government tier; regional spending, plans and delegated regulations do not make them autonomous lawmaking parliaments under the agreed rule.
frameworks.source_review: Primary constitutional/statutory text or the responsible institution’s description; translated text and source-version limitations are identified below.

frameworks.assessment: Constitution Article 110 identifies qark as the regional coordination/harmonisation tier composed from municipalities. Act 139/2015 assigns development-policy coordination and norms/standards for its allocated functions. These twelve indirectly composed county councils are administrative coordination bodies, despite generally binding decisions, budgets and public meetings; they do not establish substantive autonomous regional legislation.
frameworks.source_review: Primary constitutional/statutory text or the responsible institution’s description; translated text and source-version limitations are identified below.
frameworks.limitations: The published 2019 consolidated local-government text supports the assigned-function distinction; current membership and every later administrative amendment are not certified.

frameworks.assessment: Constitution Article 108 and Regional Councils Act section 28 assign regional councils development planning, delegated executive powers, settlement administration and coordination/advice. Limited delegated by-laws and revenue functions do not establish autonomous general regional legislation. These fourteen councils are excluded; the National Council is a separate national parliamentary chamber.
frameworks.source_review: Primary constitutional/statutory text or the responsible institution’s description; translated text and source-version limitations are identified below.
frameworks.limitations: The readable Act consolidation is dated 2013; this scope decision rests on the regional administrative allocation, not a claim of no subsequent changes or no by-law authority.

frameworks.assessment: The Local Government Act and the government’s National Decentralisation Policy classify district councils within local government, responsible for devolved services, district planning and coordination. These are not additional provincial or autonomous lawmaking parliaments. Apply the local/service-government exclusion to all ten districts.
frameworks.source_review: Primary constitutional/statutory text or the responsible institution’s description; translated text and source-version limitations are identified below.
frameworks.limitations: The original Act predates district-council amendments; the policy explicitly describes the amended district tier. Neither is used as evidence of current councillors or current service delivery.

frameworks.assessment: Local Public Administration Act 436/2006 Article 43 assigns raion councils budget/property, services/tariffs, infrastructure, development plans, institutions and administrative appointments. Those are the second-level local administration’s assigned functions, rather than autonomous regional lawmaking. Exclude the 32 ordinary raion councils; Gagauzia and the de facto Transnistrian institution have separate reviews.
frameworks.source_review: Primary constitutional/statutory text or the responsible institution’s description; translated text and source-version limitations are identified below.
frameworks.limitations: Their normative administrative decisions and elected/budgetary powers are acknowledged. This is not a blanket exclusion of every institution grouped under Moldova.

frameworks.assessment: Constitution Articles 57–63 and the revised 2020 Units and Governance Act Articles 4, 6, 9 and 35 define aimag/capital CRKs as local self-governing organs resolving assigned economic/social functions and supervising governors’ implementation. These local administrative/service decisions and budgets do not establish a separate autonomous general lawmaking legislature. Exclude the 21 aimag councils and capital council under the local-government rule.
frameworks.source_review: Primary constitutional/statutory text or the responsible institution’s description; translated text and source-version limitations are identified below.
frameworks.limitations: The law portal labels its English text an unofficial translation. Khural terminology alone does not equate these organs with the national State Great Khural.

frameworks.assessment: Constitution Articles 71–78 describe regional democratic councils as local democratic organs for area management/development. The Local Democratic Organs framework and published delegation order concern local-authority administration and district by-laws. Binding local decisions, elected membership and development budgets do not establish autonomous general regional legislative powers. Exclude ten RDCs under the local/administrative-government rule.
frameworks.source_review: Primary constitutional/statutory text or the responsible institution’s description; translated text and source-version limitations are identified below.
frameworks.limitations: The 2004 delegation order is a concrete historical illustration, not a complete present consolidation of every RDC function. The national parliamentary service remains separately eligible.

frameworks.assessment: Constitution Article 113 describes the regional council’s normative, resolving and scrutiny functions within regional government. The current consolidated regional-government Act 19.175 Articles 16, 20, 28 and 36 confines regional regulations and decisions to allocated administration, development, planning and budget. These sixteen administrative regional councils are outside the autonomous general legislative tier covered by this catalogue.
frameworks.source_review: Primary constitutional/statutory text or the responsible institution’s description; translated text and source-version limitations are identified below.
frameworks.limitations: Normative authority and direct election are acknowledged; this is not a claim that a council has no binding powers. Use the current February 2026 consolidation, not the former intendente model as current institutional evidence.

frameworks.assessment: Constitution Article 18(3), (5) and (6) establishes elected regional representative councils and autonomous regional regulations. Regional Government Act 23/2014 Articles 96–101 gives provincial DPRDs regional regulation-making, budget and oversight functions. These provincial legislatures pass the regional-ordinance scope gate, rather than merely administering assigned services.
frameworks.source_review: Primary constitutional/statutory text or the responsible institution’s description; translated text and source-version limitations are identified below.
frameworks.limitations: Article 18B preserves special/autonomous arrangements. Aceh qanun/DPRA, Yogyakarta privileges, Jakarta’s transitional name/status and the Papuan DPRP/DPRK/MRP distinctions require exact institution and event identification before any viewing-service addition. An MRP cultural consultative council or a national DPR hearing about a province is not its provincial legislature. The base Act is used for structural powers, not as a complete current consolidation of each special statute.

frameworks.assessment: Local Autonomy Act Articles 28, 32, 47 and 49 establish first-level City/Do councils’ ordinances, budget/accounts, executive inspection and veto/reconsideration machinery. They qualify under the regional-ordinance rule; rights/obligations/penalties require statutory authority. Special self-governing provinces retain their separate enabling Acts. Ordinary Si/Gun/Gu municipal councils are not included.
frameworks.source_review: Primary constitutional/statutory text or the responsible institution’s description; translated text and source-version limitations are identified below.
frameworks.limitations: The Local Autonomy Act viewer includes the 5 March 2026 consolidated-special-city amendments. Jeju’s published English special Act is a 2024 translation; Gangwon/Jeonbuk/Jeju current provider and special-statute details remain publication gates. Gwangju and Jeollanam are retained separately as predecessor records, not current councils.

frameworks.assessment: Gwangju Metropolitan Council and Jeollanam-do Council were predecessor legislatures. The official successor government and current council establish their merger into Jeonnam–Gwangju Integrated Special City on 1 July 2026. Retain these two records for archive provenance and route current research to the successor; do not count both as active current legislatures.
frameworks.source_review: Primary constitutional/statutory text or the responsible institution’s description; translated text and source-version limitations are identified below.
frameworks.limitations: Institutional succession is distinct from scope exclusion. Historical recordings retain their original council identity; no current viewing service is inferred from the merger.

frameworks.assessment: Constitution Articles 299–300 and Departmental Regime Act 2200/2022 Article 19 give departmental assemblies general ordinances, subsidiary police norm-making outside reserved national law, taxation/budget and executive scrutiny. These substantive binding regional norms meet the regional-ordinance rule despite their constitutional politico-administrative designation. The 32 departmental assemblies qualify; capital municipal councils do not qualify by analogy.
frameworks.source_review: Primary constitutional/statutory text or the responsible institution’s description; translated text and source-version limitations are identified below.
frameworks.limitations: This does not equate departmental ordinances with sovereign national statutes or certify any stream. San Andrés retains its special ethnic/territorial framework; only its departmental assembly is covered here.

frameworks.assessment: Constitution Articles 313 and 322 place Bogotá’s district council in the capital municipal/district regime. Its acuerdos, local taxes, budget and municipal police functions do not give it the separate departmental-assembly capacity evaluated under Articles 299–300. Apply the ordinary municipal exclusion despite Bogotá’s capital and district status.
frameworks.source_review: Primary constitutional/statutory text or the responsible institution’s description; translated text and source-version limitations are identified below.

frameworks.assessment: Constitution Articles 169–173 entrust district household regulation to district councils. Regional Organs Act Articles 12–13 assigns district ordinances and executive information/scrutiny; its financial chapter adds district budgets. These ten first-level councils pass the regional-ordinance gate; village/resort councils do not follow by analogy.
frameworks.source_review: Primary constitutional/statutory text or the responsible institution’s description; translated text and source-version limitations are identified below.
frameworks.limitations: The readable Regional Organs Act reproduction is consolidated to 2002, checked with the government’s 2025 constitutional publication. This confirms the legislative class, not every currently implemented financial mechanism or an actual sitting. Development consultations or a commissioner’s executive video are not legislative proceedings.

frameworks.assessment: Constitution Article 154G empowers each provincial council to make provincial statutes on the Ninth Schedule Provincial Council List; Article 154F establishes a Board of Ministers responsible to that council. These nine are constitutionally devolved legislatures, separate from municipal, urban and Pradeshiya Sabha local councils.
frameworks.source_review: Primary constitutional/statutory text or the responsible institution’s description; translated text and source-version limitations are identified below.
frameworks.limitations: Constitutional eligibility does not establish that an elected council is currently sitting. Expired/dissolved councils, delayed elections and governor administration require a current institutional-activity check before a live/current claim. Governor/executive meetings must not substitute for elected council proceedings.

frameworks.assessment: Bangsamoro Autonomy Act 49 (Local Governance Code) preserves provincial sanggunians’ ordinances, appropriation/revenue measures, regulatory penalties, executive veto/override and review of component municipal ordinances. These five provincial boards qualify under the same substantive provincial-ordinance criterion as the other Philippine provinces, using their own applicable code.
frameworks.source_review: Primary constitutional/statutory text or the responsible institution’s description; translated text and source-version limitations are identified below.
frameworks.limitations: This is not the Bangsamoro Parliament itself and does not include ordinary municipal/barangay councils. BAA93/2026 concerns Special Geographic Area authority and is not evidence of a new provincial board; confirm exact province and institutional activity before media publication.

frameworks.assessment: Revised Constitution Article II establishes the Fono’s Senate and House and gives them legislation on territorial subjects, budget and revenue machinery, subject to the territorial constitution and applicable federal law. This is a territorial legislature, not an ordinary municipal council.
frameworks.source_review: Primary constitutional/statutory text or the responsible institution’s description; translated text and source-version limitations are identified below.
frameworks.limitations: The Fono’s constitutionally different selection arrangements and territorial relationship must be retained. Do not assume every senator is elected by the same direct popular method as representatives.

frameworks.assessment: Commonwealth Constitution Article II section 1 vests rightful legislative subjects in the Northern Marianas Commonwealth Legislature, comprising Senate and House. It qualifies as a territorial/commonwealth legislature, subject to the Covenant and federal relationship, not as a US state.
frameworks.source_review: Primary constitutional/statutory text or the responsible institution’s description; translated text and source-version limitations are identified below.
frameworks.limitations: The constitutional PDF includes historical composition provisions; this establishes powers, not current chamber membership or working broadcasts.

frameworks.assessment: The Legislature’s institutional explanation and Revised Organic Act framework identify the elected unicameral Legislature as the territorial lawmaking branch, passing laws subject to gubernatorial veto, federal law and the US Constitution. It qualifies as a territorial legislature.
frameworks.source_review: Primary constitutional/statutory text or the responsible institution’s description; translated text and source-version limitations are identified below.

frameworks.assessment: DC Code section 1-203.02 gives District legislative power over all rightful subjects within the District subject to constitutional/Home Rule limits and congressional reservation. This is the special federal-district legislature, with substantive District Acts; it qualifies separately from ordinary US city councils.
frameworks.source_review: Primary constitutional/statutory text or the responsible institution’s description; translated text and source-version limitations are identified below.
frameworks.limitations: Retain federal-district status and congressional review/reserved powers. It is not a state legislature or a basis for including ordinary municipal councils.

frameworks.assessment: The Dutch Government identifies Bonaire, Saba and Sint Eustatius as public bodies similar to European municipalities, outside provincial organisation. WOLBES establishes island councils and local ordinances/scrutiny; this municipal public-body regime is distinct from the legislative constituent countries and Dutch provincial tier. Apply the ordinary municipal exclusion, retaining their special Caribbean public-body status.
frameworks.source_review: Primary constitutional/statutory text or the responsible institution’s description; translated text and source-version limitations are identified below.
frameworks.limitations: Sint Eustatius’ elected administration was restored in stages and the restoration Act ceased on 1 September 2024. Do not perpetuate the former commissioner administration or mislabel these islands as constituent countries.

frameworks.assessment: Special Status Act 344/1994 Articles 11–12 expressly empowers the People’s Assembly to adopt local laws in allocated autonomous fields, with budget and institutional control. Gagauzia qualifies as an autonomous legislature, separately from ordinary Moldovan raion councils.
frameworks.source_review: Primary constitutional/statutory text or the responsible institution’s description; translated text and source-version limitations are identified below.
frameworks.limitations: Use the special statute for the lawmaking distinction, not as certification that every original appointment/security competence survives subsequent constitutional judgments. Current membership, elections and broadcast identity require fresh institution-specific checks.

frameworks.assessment: The institution’s published constitutional text distinguishes the Supreme Council from local soviets and assigns it laws, budget and executive-control powers. It passes the functional legislature test as a de facto institution, separately from Moldova’s administrative district councils.
frameworks.source_review: Primary constitutional/statutory text or the responsible institution’s description; translated text and source-version limitations are identified below.
frameworks.limitations: The institution publishes a text consolidated to 10 July 2025. Its constitutional sovereignty claims are the source’s claims, not project recognition; preserve de facto/disputed status and the audit grouping as a research association. No current stream or institutional legitimacy is inferred.

frameworks.assessment: The Assembly’s published Constitution Articles 63 and 65 and current competence explanation establish lawmaking, budget, government election/no-confidence and oversight. The Assembly passes the functional legislature criterion and is separately identified rather than treated as an ordinary Serbian province council.
frameworks.source_review: Primary constitutional/statutory text or the responsible institution’s description; translated text and source-version limitations are identified below.
frameworks.limitations: Retain disputed/separate-status context and neutral territorial presentation. The ledger’s Serbia grouping is a historical research association, not a sovereignty determination or an assertion that this is a Serbian subnational institution.

frameworks.assessment: The de facto Ombudsman’s current institutional statement explicitly cites Constitution Articles 4 and 78 assigning lawmaking to Cumhuriyet Meclisi; the constitutional text also assigns budget and ministerial scrutiny. This is a functional de facto legislature, distinct from Cyprus’ ordinary district service organisations.
frameworks.source_review: Primary constitutional/statutory text or the responsible institution’s description; translated text and source-version limitations are identified below.
frameworks.limitations: Preserve de facto/disputed status; this is not recognition of sovereignty. The parliament entry route timed out during research. The authority statement establishes the class, not a working viewing route; do not substitute the Republic of Türkiye’s Constitution, which search results also returned.

frameworks.assessment: The Assembly’s current explanation identifies primary Acts within the Northern Ireland Act’s transferred competence, with committee legislation and government scrutiny. Northern Ireland is a devolved legislature, not a local council.
frameworks.source_review: Primary constitutional/statutory text or the responsible institution’s description; translated text and source-version limitations are identified below.
frameworks.limitations: Excepted/reserved matters and competence limits remain. This resolves a stale authority label on an already catalogued institution, not a new source.

frameworks.assessment: Alderney’s current official election/institutional explanation identifies the States as its legislature, debating legislation, major expenditure and policies with responsible executive committees. It passes the Crown Dependency legislature criterion, separately from Guernsey’s transferred services.
frameworks.source_review: Primary constitutional/statutory text or the responsible institution’s description; translated text and source-version limitations are identified below.
frameworks.limitations: Alderney is within the Bailiwick of Guernsey, not part of the United Kingdom. The ledger’s country grouping is a research association. Royal assent and transferred Guernsey functions limit its powers without making it a municipal council.

frameworks.assessment: The UK Supreme Court’s Barclay judgments identify Chief Pleas as Sark’s legislature and explain its lawmaking/assent relationship. Current Chief Pleas material publishes its legislation, budget, committees and 2026 sittings. It qualifies as a Crown Dependency legislature, rather than an ordinary council.
frameworks.source_review: Primary constitutional/statutory text or the responsible institution’s description; translated text and source-version limitations are identified below.
frameworks.limitations: Do not copy historical membership/Seneschal arrangements from the 2009 judgment as current. Sark is within the Bailiwick of Guernsey, not part of the UK. Proceedings and current room/provider identity still need validation.

frameworks.assessment: Constitution section 47 gives the Governor with the advice and consent of the Assembly lawmaking for Anguilla; sections 49 onward establish bill and assembly procedures. It is a territorial legislature, subject to assent/reserved powers, not an advisory island council.
frameworks.source_review: Primary constitutional/statutory text or the responsible institution’s description; translated text and source-version limitations are identified below.
frameworks.limitations: The original constitutional text is used for the foundational legislative distinction, not every later membership/name amendment or a current stream.

frameworks.assessment: Constitution sections 37 and 50 empower the Governor with the advice and consent of the Legislative Assembly to enact territorial Ordinances; its budget and assembly procedures form a legislative institution. It qualifies as a territorial legislature.
frameworks.source_review: Primary constitutional/statutory text or the responsible institution’s description; translated text and source-version limitations are identified below.
frameworks.limitations: Retain territorial/disputed sovereignty context and assent/reserved powers; the audit grouping does not settle sovereignty.

frameworks.assessment: Constitution sections 47 and 60 establish a Legislature including the Legislative Council and lawmaking for St Helena; sections 97–106 provide taxation, appropriations and public accounts scrutiny. It qualifies, separately from Ascension and Tristan’s advisory island councils.
frameworks.source_review: Primary constitutional/statutory text or the responsible institution’s description; translated text and source-version limitations are identified below.
frameworks.limitations: The 2021 ministerial-system amendment affects executive arrangements; use the revised text for current operation. The foundational legislature/appropriation provisions are not evidence of a working broadcast.

frameworks.assessment: Constitution sections 151 and 216 place lawmaking in the Governor after consultation with the respective Island Council and expressly allow the Governor to disregard its advice. These councils are consultative island-administration bodies, rather than representative lawmaking assemblies. Geographic remoteness and a constitutional chapter titled Legislature do not transfer that power to the councils.
frameworks.source_review: Primary constitutional/statutory text or the responsible institution’s description; translated text and source-version limitations are identified below.

frameworks.assessment: Constitution section 36 gives the Governor lawmaking after consultation with the Island Council, rather than enactment by that council. The UN’s 2026 territorial working paper confirms this division and the council’s local-government role. It is outside the representative-legislature scope.
frameworks.source_review: Primary constitutional/statutory text or the responsible institution’s description; translated text and source-version limitations are identified below.
frameworks.limitations: The council’s involvement and any delegated local rules are acknowledged; it is not the Governor’s substantive territorial legislative authority.

frameworks.assessment: Niue Constitution Articles 28 and 34–36 give the Assembly laws and constitutional amendment, while Articles 56–60 establish legislative control of public revenues. It qualifies as a self-governing free-associated state legislature, not a New Zealand regional council.
frameworks.source_review: Primary constitutional/statutory text or the responsible institution’s description; translated text and source-version limitations are identified below.
frameworks.limitations: Retain free association and Niue’s separate constitutional identity. The New Zealand research grouping is not subnational status.

frameworks.assessment: Tokelau Act sections 3A–3F and the official government explanation give General Fono rules for peace, order and good government, including taxes. That broad territorial norm-making and national-budget role passes the legislature criterion. This is General Fono, not the individual village Taupulega.
frameworks.source_review: Primary constitutional/statutory text or the responsible institution’s description; translated text and source-version limitations are identified below.
frameworks.limitations: Use the enacted Tokelau Act, not a draft Constitution in the unsuccessful self-determination package, as the operative legal basis. Rule hierarchy, national/village powers and New Zealand’s retained responsibilities remain distinct.

frameworks.assessment: COCOF’s institutional explanation distinguishes its transferred legislative competencies from its role implementing French Community decrees. Its francophone parliamentary assembly adopts decrees with force of law in transferred fields and controls its responsible College and budget. It qualifies, separately from municipal councils and the Flemish Community Commission’s regulatory role.
frameworks.source_review: Primary constitutional/statutory text or the responsible institution’s description; translated text and source-version limitations are identified below.
frameworks.limitations: This is language/community-based institutional coverage in Brussels; do not portray it as an ordinary territorial province or duplicate the whole Brussels parliament under a second name.

frameworks.assessment: Regional Assembly Act section 31 directly authorises Rodrigues Regional Assembly Regulations within its devolved responsibility, effective in Rodrigues and subordinate to national law. Its budget, executive and no-confidence provisions support that territorial legislative role. It qualifies under the regional-ordinance rule.
frameworks.source_review: Primary constitutional/statutory text or the responsible institution’s description; translated text and source-version limitations are identified below.
frameworks.limitations: Section 30 Bills still require national enactment: do not repeat the institutional introduction’s broad wording as unfettered primary lawmaking. Eligibility rests on section 31’s actual island-wide regulations plus budget/executive control.

frameworks.assessment: The Tobago House of Assembly Act section 29 allows proposing/adopting Bills but requires Cabinet introduction and national Parliament enactment for an Assembly Law. Its own votes do not enact those laws. Its substantial devolved administration, budget and scrutiny therefore do not establish autonomous territorial lawmaking under the present catalogue rule.
frameworks.source_review: Primary constitutional/statutory text or the responsible institution’s description; translated text and source-version limitations are identified below.
frameworks.limitations: The Assembly-hosted base text is consolidated only to 2013. Act 1/2026 was read and changes secretary numbers/quorum, not section 29’s enactment route. This exclusion is a project scope interpretation despite its Legislature branding; reopen on enacted substantive autonomy powers, not a proposed reform.

frameworks.assessment: CGCT L4422-16 gives Corsica assigned regulatory powers and rights to propose adaptations to national legislation; proposing legislation is not autonomous enactment. The 2026 constitutional-autonomy dossier is a pending reform, not the current statutory power. Under current verified law the Assembly remains outside the substantive autonomous-lawmaking scope.
frameworks.source_review: Primary constitutional/statutory text or the responsible institution’s description; translated text and source-version limitations are identified below.
frameworks.limitations: The National Assembly adopted a first-reading constitutional text on 23 June 2026. That does not establish completed constitutional amendment, enabling organic legislation or commenced legislative powers. Reopen on enacted change.

frameworks.assessment: Constitution Article 73 expressly excludes Réunion from the third/fourth-paragraph rule-setting derogation; the region retains ordinary assigned regional administration and regulatory powers, with possible second-paragraph adaptations. Those do not establish an autonomous general regional legislature under this scope rule.

frameworks.assessment: Law 2026-574 of 30 June 2026 actually grants the Assembly Article 73 rule-setting authority in energy and water/sanitation until its next general renewal, including legislative-domain rules. Together with its territorial budget and executive scrutiny, this is a concrete devolved normative mandate beyond ordinary regional administration and passes the scope gate.

frameworks.assessment: Decree 57-811 Articles 40–42 gives the Territorial Assembly territorial regulations in allocated fields and permits amendment/repeal of earlier laws/decrees treated as territorial regulations; budget and territorial deliberations are separately assigned. It qualifies under the territorial-ordinance rule, not through the three customary kingdom/circonscription councils.

This customary territorial norm-making and control passes the legislature criterion. The consultative Nokora council and ordinary municipal bodies are distinct.

frameworks.assessment: Executive Decree 228/1998 Articles 10–13 gives General Congress decisions binding across the comarca, its territorial statutes/resolutions and appointment/control of authorities. Articles 30–36 distinguish its finances and budget from the national allocation. These territorial normative and control powers pass the customary-legislature criterion; its religious/cultural Traditional Congress is a different body.

frameworks.assessment: Law 16/1953 recognises General Congress’s customary territorial jurisdiction. Congress’s own Fundamental Law/statutory framework, tourism regulation and published budget resolutions demonstrate territorial rules, controls/removal of executive officials and budget approval. These are substantive customary territorial governance powers, not merely an advocacy council; General Congress passes the functional criterion.
frameworks.source_review: Primary constitutional/statutory text or the responsible institution’s description; translated text and source-version limitations are identified below.
frameworks.limitations: The budget resolutions are dated historical examples of exercised authority, not the current budget. The political General Congress must remain distinct from the General Congress of Culture and individual community assemblies.

frameworks.assessment: Organic Charter Decree 414/2008 Articles 9, 12, 26–27 and 89 establishes binding comarca-wide decisions and residual customary rule-making, executive reporting/removal and financial misconduct controls; Article 82 provides Congress revenues. Those substantive territorial norms and accountable financial/executive machinery pass the customary-legislature criterion. This is General Congress, not its ordinary corregimiento representative or local village congress.
frameworks.source_review: Primary constitutional/statutory text or the responsible institution’s description; translated text and source-version limitations are identified below.
frameworks.limitations: The Charter establishes revenues and accountability, not an explicit modern annual appropriation procedure in the text reviewed. Preserve that distinction. A project-consent resolution alone was insufficient; the enacted Charter resolves the scope gate.

frameworks.assessment: Organic Charter Decree 194/1999 Articles 52 and 57 makes General Congress resolutions binding and authorises general coexistence/family norms, control of funds, commissions and chief/board reporting. Articles 58–59 require property and administration accounts. These customary territorial norms and executive/financial controls pass the legislature criterion, separately from the people-wide Buglé congress.
